items.title: Computer-aided diagnosis for lung cancer screening
points: Posted by Atilla Kiraly, Software Engineer, and Rory Pilgrim, Product Manager, Google Research Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related deaths globally with 1.8 million deaths reported in 2020.

Lung cancer screening via computed tomography (CT), which provides a detailed 3D image of the lungs, has been shown to reduce mortality in high-risk populations by at least 20% by detecting potential signs of cancers earlier.

The United States Preventive Services Task Force recently expanded lung cancer screening recommendations by roughly 80% , which is expected to increase screening access for women and racial and ethnic minority groups.
